svg.title: Direct invocation state: one bounded structural change
svg.desc: The baseline wraps a captured continuation in SynchronousSink. The candidate uses an immutable per-pipeline DirectStage plan and a fresh DirectInvocation with owner, nextStage and output references, clearing its three invocation references in finally. Public entry-point and session/async source regions match byte for byte. Source expressions are not physical heap-object counts; guard equivalence also relies on lifecycle tests.

svg.text: Combine the state. Preserve the boundary.
One production file changes; public entry-point and session / async source remains byte-identical.
Pipeline.process → dispatch → processor.process → guarded output → next stage
Detach the owner and downstream delegate.
The builder still snapshots processor references.
Source plan: N nodes + N-reference array
No per-call frame, output or owner fields.
No plan when hasAsync is true.
Live owner + nextStage = null → terminal output.
owner = null identifies a retired invocation.
owner = null / nextStage = null / output = null
Plan setup cost is measured separately.
A retired handle is never pooled or reactivated.
PRESERVED BEHAVIOR / VERIFIED BY LIFECYCLE FIXTURES
Nested calls, post-output exceptions and retained handles remain part of the correctness boundary.
Checked source: identical public methods / known plan setup / identical session and async suffix.
Source expressions do not count physical heap objects; inlining and escape analysis may reshape allocation.
Use paired JMH time and B/op for measured effects. This source check is not a formal equivalence proof.
No sink pooling, session scheduler change, generation-fence change or media-constructor change.
